deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics and no derivations. It is not a working sheet by Riemann. It is an editorial note in another hand, written after Riemann's death in 1866. It is almost certainly a draft of the editorial remark printed in Riemann's Gesammelte Mathematische Werke (1876, editors Dedekind and H. Weber). The note sits beside the memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', which deals with minimal surfaces and Plateau's problem. The bundle name 'R.Minimal' fits this identification.

The note says the following:
(1) In April 1866 Riemann handed the manuscript to Karl Hattendorff to work up and publish.
(2) By Riemann's own statement the manuscript was then already 5 to 6 years old, which places its composition around 1860-61.
(3) Hattendorff's first edition appeared in 1867 with his own historical introduction. It was published in Abh. d. Kgl. Ges. d. Wiss. zu Göttingen, Bd. 13.
(4) For the collected works Hattendorff kindly re-edited the text (a 'neue Redaction'). The historical introduction was dropped because it did not come from Riemann.

The writer first began 'wurde im April 1866' and struck it out. He also struck a 'Herrn' before 'Hattendorff' in line 6.

The note's value is bibliographic and historical. It dates the minimal-surface work to about 1860-61. It also records that the published text is an editor's reworking (Hattendorff, twice) rather than Riemann's own wording.
errors: There are no mathematical statements to check.

The historical claims agree with the known publication history: Hattendorff's edition appeared in 1867 in Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, and a revised version appeared in the 1876 Werke without the historical introduction.
